=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are tightly grouped at the apex, forming a rosette-like structure)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no visible teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (narrow, elongated with a pointed apex and broad base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to the petiole, wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are distinct and run parallel to each other, forming a net-like pattern)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or pubescence on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, barely visible)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is light green, matching the petiole)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate or milky sap visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; not applicable for Fabaceae, but not observed)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils present)

F. Notes: Multiple images show the same seedling from various angles, confirming a whorled arrangement of simple, lanceolate leaves with entire margins and shiny surfaces. Some leaf margins show minor damage (e.g., small holes or missing sections), but no clear signs of herbivory or disease. The seedling is marked with a pink tag, likely for field identification. No flowers, fruits, or roots are visible. The surrounding litter includes dry palm fronds and leaf debris, but habitat conditions are not inferred.
